title: PowerPoint for business analysts on Mac: faster decks with masters, Copilot and voice
metaTitle: PowerPoint for Business Analysts on Mac: Masters and Copilot
description: PowerPoint for business analysts on Mac: masters, reused slides, Copilot costs and voice help with Lazur. Mac menu steps for Microsoft 365, updated 2026.
targetKeyword: powerpoint for business analysts on mac
intro: PowerPoint for business analysts on Mac means building client and internal decks in PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac. Start every deck from a slide master, reuse slides that already work, and write new content only after the layout is set. This guide covers those habits, the Mac-specific gaps, what Copilot costs and how Lazur helps by voice while you work.
tldr: Build from a slide master. Use View > Slide Master so every slide shares fonts, colors and layouts.
On Mac, layout names can stay stale in Normal view after you edit a master. Test a copy before you rely on it.
Copilot may not come with your Microsoft 365 plan, and the Business add-on has its own price. Check before you budget.
Ask Lazur where a button is, or to walk you through a step, while you keep working in PowerPoint.

blocks.text: What PowerPoint for business analysts on Mac looks like day to day

Most of your PowerPoint time goes to a few jobs. You paste a table or chart from Excel onto a slide. You add a title, a takeaway and a source line. Then you copy a slide that worked last month and swap in new numbers. Mac users do this with the same habits as Windows users. The menus sit in slightly different places, so expect small surprises.

Research on office work points the same way. A secondary source citing a GfK survey for Made in Office says employees spend about 20 hours a month in PowerPoint. About 8 of those hours go to formatting. That survey covered office workers in general, not business analysts. Treat the figure as a rough signal, not a benchmark for your team.

Your own log will tell you more. Track one week of deck work and note which tasks eat the most minutes. Alignment, font and copy work usually hides in the margins. It rarely shows up as one big task, so it is easy to miss.
Build decks from a slide master, not from scratch

The slide master is the biggest time saver in PowerPoint. It holds the fonts, colors, logo and layouts for every slide in the deck. Change the master once, and every slide that uses it can update. Microsoft says Slide Master view keeps colors, fonts, headings, logos and other styles consistent.

You can also edit or delete layouts, apply themes, set orientation and configure footers from that view. On a Mac, open it with View > Slide Master. Insert Slide Master adds a master. Delete removes a layout. Slide Size > Page Setup sets orientation. Close Master exits.

items: Open the template or deck you want to standardize, then choose View > Slide Master.
Select the top master slide to change the theme fonts and colors for the whole deck.
Edit one layout, such as Title and Content, and check it on a sample slide.
Use Slide Size > Page Setup if the deck needs a different orientation.
Choose Close Master on the Slide Master tab when you finish.
Save the file with File > Save as Template if the team will reuse it.

blocks.text: Build the master before you build the content. If you change a layout later, existing slides may not pick up the change. Reapply the layout to each slide. That step saves you from fixing the same title box on every slide by hand.

Keep one master file for each client or team. Name it clearly, with the month and a version label. A shared master with a clear name beats three near-copies sitting in old email threads. Ask the client for their template file if they have one, and build from that instead.

Watch for locked layouts. Some client templates arrive with layouts that cannot be edited. If a layout is locked, do not copy it into your own file and hope for the best. Ask the client's team for the source template, or build a plain layout that matches their fonts and colors.
Fix layout names that do not update on Mac

This is a Mac quirk that trips up teams. A December 2025 question on Microsoft's Q&A forum says correct layout names show in Slide Master view but do not update in Normal view on Mac. The thread shows no confirmed fix. The one answer came from an unidentified user, not a moderator.

That answer suggests reapplying the layouts or duplicating them. Try that on a copy of the deck first. Rename one layout, then check the name in Normal view. If the name still lags, duplicate the layout and use the copy. Keep the original file until the new template passes your check.

blocks.title: Test before you share
blocks.text: The layout-name workaround is unverified. Check the name in Normal view on a copy before you send a template to your team.
Reuse existing slides without breaking the design

Business analysts reuse slides more than almost anyone. The same GfK-based secondary source says about 78% of decks are built from existing slides. It also says about 70% of presentations do not follow corporate design standards. Those two numbers explain a lot of the mixed fonts you see in shared decks.

Reuse slides in a controlled way. Copy the slides you need from the older deck with ⌘C, then paste them with ⌘V into your master-based file. Right after pasting, open the Paste Options control. Choose the option that uses the destination theme, so the slide picks up your template's fonts and colors.

Then reapply the layout. A pasted slide can keep a layout from the old file. Reapplying it links the slide to the layout in your master. If the title box still looks wrong, the old master is the cause, not the slide.

Use fonts your client also has. A deck built on a font the client does not own will change on their machine. Ask IT for a standard font list, or stick to the fonts already in your template. This matters most for client decks that travel.
Paste Excel tables and charts without the mess

Most analyst decks start in Excel. Copying a table into PowerPoint is quick, but the result can look like a spreadsheet pasted onto a slide. Decide first whether the audience needs to edit the numbers. If not, paste it as a picture, which keeps the look fixed. If yes, keep it as a table and set the font size to match the rest of the deck.

Do not resize a pasted table by dragging one corner alone. Hold Shift while you drag, so the proportions stay the same. Then check that the row text still fits. Font size is usually the fix, not a smaller box.

Charts raise the same question. A chart pasted with its data keeps a link to the source workbook. A chart pasted as a picture stays fixed. Pick the type that matches how the deck will travel. If the deck goes to a client who will not open Excel, use a picture of the chart.
Where the time goes: a rough budget for one deck

The chart compares the 20 hours with the 8 hours from the secondary source. The gap is the part you can cut. For many analysts, the cut comes from masters and reused layouts, not from better content. The source covers general office workers, so read the bars as a prompt, not a result.

Track your own week to make the picture real. Write down the minutes you spend on content and the minutes on alignment, fonts and copying. Compare the two totals at the end of the week. The split matters more than the total.
Copilot in PowerPoint for Mac: what it does for a deck

Copilot is the main new feature in the 2026 release notes for PowerPoint for Mac. Version 16.109, build 26051019, arrived on May 12, 2026. It added the ability to edit your document with Copilot. Copilot can generate slides, update content, improve layouts and polish design from a plain-language prompt.

To start a new deck, open a new presentation. Select the Copilot icon at the bottom right. Choose an AI model, or leave the setting on Auto. Pick a brand kit if your company requires one. Then describe the deck in plain words.

items: Copilot may ask about the audience, length, template and imagery.
You can answer those questions or skip them.
Copilot builds on the template you select, and its layouts come from that file.
Start from your organization's standard template if you have one.

blocks.text: The template step matters most. Copilot keeps the theme and design of the file you pick. Start from a blank file and the output looks generic. Start from your master and the draft is much closer to your house style. That one choice cuts the most rework.

Treat the first draft as a rough cut. Check the slide order first, then the titles, then the numbers, then the design. Fix design last, because it changes most often. A draft that reads well can still have a wrong figure on slide four.

With Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), Copilot can connect to a brand kit. It can apply branded templates, insert brand-approved images and check brand compliance. These features only work if your IT team has set up the brand kit first.
What Copilot costs for one analyst

rows: Shown as originally $21.00. Auto-renews. Promo runs July 1 to December 31, 2026, first year only, with an annual commitment.
Monthly billing. The promo needs an annual commitment, so it does not cover monthly billing.
blocks.caption: Prices from Microsoft's Copilot pricing page.

blocks.text: Two cautions apply. First, Microsoft's Copilot help page says Copilot might not be included with your Microsoft 365 subscription. It also depends on your organization's settings. Second, these prices are for the Business add-on. Some third-party blogs quote other figures. Use Microsoft's pricing page as the reference.

Budget Copilot as a per-seat cost. Multiply the monthly price by the number of analysts who will use it. Compare that with the hours your team saves on formatting. Only the saved hours can justify the cost, and they depend on how often you build decks.
Check your license before you count on editing

Microsoft's known-issues page says that from July 13, 2026, some Microsoft 365 subscribers on macOS may be in reduced functionality mode. In that mode you can open and print files. You cannot edit, save or create them. That date has already passed as of this writing.

Microsoft does not say how this is enforced. So do not assume your copy works. Open a deck, change one word and save it to a copy. If the save fails or the option is missing, contact your IT admin before a deadline.

blocks.title: Check before a deadline
blocks.text: A deck that opens but will not save is a deck you cannot send. Run the edit and save test a day before a client review, not on the morning of it.
Version notes that change how decks behave

items: 16.107, March 10, 2026: when you save a .pptx with SVG graphics, PowerPoint no longer renders and saves a PNG with each one.
16.109, build 26051019, May 12, 2026: Copilot in PowerPoint arrived, with prompt-based editing.
16.114.3, build 26102720, October 27, 2026: Microsoft lists quality and performance improvements only.

blocks.text: The SVG change matters if your deck relies on PNG fallbacks. Open the file in an older viewer before you send it. Keep a PNG copy of key icons if the receiving team uses older software.

Find your version with PowerPoint > About PowerPoint. Compare it with Microsoft's release notes. Microsoft's known-issues page also lists an automatic sensitivity label policy that does not work in PowerPoint for Mac. It was under investigation as of July 2026, so ask IT if your company depends on automatic labels.
Mac and Windows naming differences

rows: Close Master on the Slide Master tab
blocks.caption: Menu names from Microsoft's slide master help page.

blocks.text: Mac and Windows share the same ideas but not always the same labels. A 2015 Slidegenius article says the Mac ribbon and menus differ slightly from Windows. Some features sit in unexpected places. That article is old. Use Microsoft's current help as the main reference.

When you search for a menu item, use the Mac wording. Search the Microsoft help page for your app version. If a Windows guide says Custom Slide Size, look for Slide Size on the Mac, then open Page Setup.
Keyboard and voice habits that save time

Mac PowerPoint uses Command shortcuts. ⌘Z undoes the last change, including a layout you did not mean to apply. ⌘C copies and ⌘V pastes, which makes slide copying quick. Learn these first, because they work the same way in most Mac apps.

items: ⌘Z: undo the last change, including a layout you did not mean to apply.
⌘C and ⌘V: copy and paste slides or shapes between decks.
⌥⌘: hold Option and Command to ask Lazur about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud.
fn: hold to dictate clean text at the cursor, in PowerPoint or any other app.

blocks.text: Voice help for analyst work in PowerPoint

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold Option and Command to ask about anything on your screen. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. It answers out loud.

Ask where something is and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it gives the next step. That fits PowerPoint well, because most menu steps are short and easy to lose.

Lazur does not click buttons for you. It does not edit files or operate other apps. It is not a plugin or add-in for PowerPoint. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

Dictation is useful for speaker notes and slide text. Hold fn, speak and release. Clean text appears at your cursor. Add the product names and acronyms your team uses to the personal dictionary once, so they come out right every time.

Dictation is not the headline feature here. Use it for the parts of a deck you would otherwise type, such as speaker notes and long titles. Use the questions for menu steps, which are where most lost minutes go.
Ask Lazur where the Close Master button is

This is the best first test. Open a deck, go to View > Slide Master, then hold Option and Command. Say, where is the Close Master button? Lazur draws a circle and a label around the button on the Slide Master tab. You still click it yourself.

Ask follow-ups while you work. Try, what does Insert Slide Master do? Or, why is my layout name not changing? Lazur answers about what is on screen. It keeps a memory of what you asked and did on your Mac, so you can pick up where you left off.
Privacy: what Lazur sends and keeps
Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

If your deck is on screen when you ask, the screenshot can show it. Check your company's policy before you share client data with any AI tool, Lazur included. Ask IT which tools are approved, and close client files during a question if the policy says so.
Mistakes that cost analysts time

items: Editing a master after you build slides, then skipping the layout reapply.
Pasting slides with the source theme, which brings in old fonts and colors.
Trusting a Copilot draft without checking every figure against the Excel source.
Skipping the license check until a deck is due.
Sending an SVG-heavy deck to older builds without opening it there first.
Searching for a Windows menu name on a Mac, then giving up.

blocks.text: Copilot drafts look finished, which makes wrong numbers easy to miss. Read every figure against its source. For numbers, the Excel side matters most. The [Excel guide for business analysts on Mac](/for/business-analysts/excel) covers the formulas and pivots that feed a deck.
A worked example: from a monthly KPI pack to a client deck

Say you get a monthly KPI pack from Excel. It has several charts, a summary slide and a risk page. Start with the master you built earlier. Duplicate the layout that fits the chart. Paste the chart, then write the title as the takeaway, not as a topic.

Ask Lazur for help where you get stuck. Ask where Slide Size is if the pack uses a wide format. Ask it to explain a placeholder you do not recognize. Dictate the speaker notes with fn, so you can talk through the logic while the slide is open.

Titles as takeaways are a habit that pays off. A title such as churn rose in two regions tells the reader what to see. A title such as churn tells them nothing. Let the title carry the point, and let the chart support it.

When the deck is ready, check the version and license notes first. If the client needs a walkthrough video, follow the [save as video steps](/how-to/save-as-a-video-in-powerpoint). Then share the file in the format the client asked for.
Speaker notes, Presenter View and alt text

Speaker notes help you keep the story straight. Add them as you build, not the night before. The [speaker notes guide](/how-to/add-speaker-notes-in-powerpoint) shows the steps. For the meeting itself, [Presenter View](/how-to/use-presenter-view-in-powerpoint) keeps your notes on your screen while the room sees only the slide.

Alt text matters too. Readers using screen readers need it, and so does your own search later. The [alt text guide](/how-to/add-alt-text-to-an-image-in-powerpoint) explains the steps for images. Write one short line that says what the picture shows, not its file name.
What to do next

items: Open a copy of your current template and check View > Slide Master.
Test one layout name in Normal view using the workaround above.
Check your Copilot plan and license with IT before you budget for it.
Ask Lazur the Close Master question once, and see whether the answer helps.

blocks.text: Download Lazur from the [download page](/download) if you want to try it on your Mac. Plans and trial terms are on the [pricing page](/pricing). The [PowerPoint page](/apps/powerpoint) lists the kinds of questions Lazur answers in this app.
Start with the master. It takes a short sitting to set up, and it pays back on every deck after that. Everything else in this guide gets easier once the master is right.

faq.question: Which PowerPoint version does this guide cover?
faq.answer: This guide covers PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac, the name Microsoft uses in its Mac help. It references version 16.109 and newer builds, including 16.114.3 from October 27, 2026. Check your own version with PowerPoint > About PowerPoint.

faq.question: How do I open Slide Master on a Mac?
faq.answer: Go to View > Slide Master. The Slide Master tab opens with the master and its layouts. Choose Close Master on that tab when you finish. Microsoft's Mac help uses that wording.

faq.question: Does PowerPoint for Mac include Copilot?
faq.answer: Copilot appears in PowerPoint for Mac from version 16.109, released May 12, 2026. Microsoft says Copilot might not be included with your Microsoft 365 subscription, and it depends on your organization's settings. Ask your admin which plan applies.

faq.question: How much does Copilot cost per user?
faq.answer: Microsoft lists Copilot Business at $18.00 per user a month when paid yearly, shown as originally $21.00. Monthly billing is $25.20 per user a month. The yearly promo runs July 1 to December 31, 2026, for the first year. Check Microsoft's pricing page for current terms.

faq.question: Why do my layout names not update on Mac?
faq.answer: A December 2025 Microsoft Q&A thread reports that Mac shows correct layout names in Slide Master view but not in Normal view. The thread shows no confirmed fix. Try reapplying or duplicating the layouts on a copy of the deck first.

faq.question: What is reduced functionality mode?
faq.answer: Microsoft's known-issues page says that from July 13, 2026, some Microsoft 365 subscribers on macOS may be in this mode. You can open and print files, but you cannot edit, save or create them. Microsoft does not say how it is enforced, so test a save on a copy.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my slides or click buttons?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. It points at things, answers out loud, guides you one click at a time and drafts text you can paste into your deck.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Are my slides sent to AI providers when I ask Lazur a question?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. If your deck is on screen, the screenshot can show it, so follow your company's policy.
